newsitem.title: USA: Marriott to acquire Renaissance Hotel.
newsitem.headline: Marriott to acquire Renaissance Hotel.

text.p: Marriott International Inc said Tuesday it had agreed to acquire Renaissance Hotel Group NV for $30 cash per share in a transaction valued at $1 billion, including transaction costs and assumption of Renaissance debt.

Washington-based Marriott said shareholders of 54 percent of Renaissance's voting stock have already agreed to the deal. It said it would launch a tender for the balance of the shares within five days.
Combined, the companies will have more than 1,300 hotels worldwide, across 10 brands, said Marriott.
It said it anticipates annual cost savings of $15 million to $20 million from the merger.
Marriott said it expects its earnings before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization rising by $75 million to $85 million in the first 12 months after the acquisition.
For 1997, however, it expects its earnings to be reduced by $0.10 to $0.14 per share.
Marriott shares closed Friday at 55-1/4, while Renaissance shares closed at 25-1/8.
Renaissance, which is based in the Netherlands, operates and franchises 150 hotels in 38 countries. Its brands include New World and Ramada.
Marriott operates about 4,700 units in the U.S. and 29 other countries, including the Marriott and Residence Inn brands.
